comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: that ratio breaks when the in-sample return is tiny or negative: 2% in and 3% out reads as 150%, and a losing training window flips the sign entirely. what does the lab flag when the in-sample window lost money?

replies.author: aureliaspes
replies.body:
Good catch, and you’re right: the ratio breaks at both ends.

Here’s how the lab handles it now:

* **In-sample window lost money:** the ratio isn’t used as a pass. The run is marked RED, “Poor result: lost money in-sample”, even if the out-of-sample stretch made a small gain. A strategy that can’t make money on the data it was tuned on hasn’t earned an out-of-sample read.
* **Too few out-of-sample trades:** under 10, a run can’t get GREEN however good the numbers look. It’s marked YELLOW with the reason.
* **Tiny positive in-sample return (your 2% → 3% case):** fair point, the ratio overstates that one. We’re looking at setting a minimum in-sample return before the ratio is shown, or comparing risk-adjusted returns (Sharpe) instead of raw returns.

How do you handle it: risk-adjusted efficiency, or a floor on the in-sample result?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: RED on an in-sample loss no matter what came after is how I'd do it too. the trade-count floor matters more than the ratio, under 30 or so out-of-sample trades a 1.5x and a 0.5x are basically the same coin flip.

replies.author: aureliaspes
replies.body: Agreed, and that’s a fair push on our floor. Right now the lab won’t give GREEN under 10 out-of-sample trades, which by your standard is still coin-flip territory. Two things we’re looking at: raising the floor towards 30, and showing the out-of-sample trade count and a bootstrapped range right next to the efficiency ratio, so a 1.5x on 12 trades doesn’t look as solid as a 1.5x on 200. Would you rather see a hard floor, or the range shown and let the trader judge?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the range, with the count right beside it. a hard floor at 30 just moves the cliff, 29 trades gets hidden and 31 looks solid. if the band is wide enough people work it out on their own.
